description: Supplement to negative-cases.json, which stays frozen. For each frozen case whose mutation breaks more than one rule, this file gives an isolated variant, where one can be built, in which the mutated bytes break only the target rule. Where isolation is impossible under the text, not_isolatable gives the reason. Every expectation comes from the specification text alone.

errata.change: inputs changed from s = 1, o = 2^56 to s = 2^56 + 1, o = 2^56; violates_only, every_other_rule_holds, quotes and sections restated
errata.reason: Section 10.3 requires one Object row per kind-0 structural row, and Section 10.2 requires structural row 0 to be the bootstrap, so o ≤ s − 1. With s = 1 that rule broke as well as the product. s = o = 2^56 would also break it. s = 2^56 + 1 keeps it and leaves 256 × o as the only overflow, since 64 × s = 2^62 + 64 fits.

errata.change: removed from variants; added to not_isolatable as overflow-10.1.2-2M-footer
errata.reason: It used B = 2, below the ParityMap minimum block size of 0xC8 (Section 10.1.2). For B ≥ 0xC8, M < 2^57, so 2M + 1 cannot overflow, and no construction that respects the minimum reaches this formula.

conventions.ISO-BOTH: Apply the parent's mutation identically to BOTH header/index copies of the sidecar (primary at block 0, tail at block H+P). Recompute each copy's canonical_metadata_hash; the two hashes are equal, because copy_kind is excluded from the hash. Then recompute each copy's header_crc64 (0xC0) and block0_crc64 (B-8). Write that hash into the footer (0x60) and recompute footer_crc64 (0x80). Write it into the ParityMap directory entry for the sidecar (key 8) and apply R-PM-PAYLOAD from negative-cases.json. Any field the footer or directory entry mirrors (H 0x38/key 6, P 0x40/key 7, total 0x48/key 5, range 0x28/0x30/keys 3-4) gets the new value there too, when that mirror has no rule of its own the value would break. A mutation confined to hash-excluded bytes (copy_kind, the reserved fields, copy_generation) changes neither the footer nor the directory. Result: the Section 9.1 primary/tail agreement, the footer comparison of Section 13.3 step 1 and the directory hash check all hold.
conventions.ISO-FAULT-FOOTER: Used when the footer mirrors the field under its own rule (primary start = 0, tail start = H + P) or with a rule the text leaves unstated (the footer's tape_uuid). The harness presents the sidecar's footer block (block 2H+P) as unreadable: it returns a medium error for that one block read and changes no byte. With no footer, the footer comparison takes no part. The Recoverer proceeds by Section 13.3 steps 2 and 3, and a Scanner in a BOT walk uses item 5. A medium error is damage, not a format violation (Section 15: 'I/O faults MUST remain distinct from format violations').
conventions.ISO-REBUILD: Used when the new value changes the sidecar's physical length. Rebuild the image with the sidecar at its new block count, then regenerate everything that depends on the prefix: the replicas' structural row for the sidecar; the ParityMap directory entry (keys 5-8); the ParityMap's canonical_map_digest (header/footer 0x58 and payload key 5), payload_sha256 and CRCs; all three replicas (payload, canonical-map, edition, layout and descriptor digests; the five component tuples; the local planned tape-file and start fields; EOD; footer observations; header-record hashes; CRCs); and both separation extents (tuples, predecessor/successor fields, descriptor digests, header-record hashes, CRCs). Every terminal LBA shifts by the change in the sidecar's block count.
conventions.UNIT: The rule can be reached only at unit level: the named computation of the named role, called with the listed inputs. The reason field says why no byte image can present these inputs while every other rule of the role holds.
conventions.expected_for_7a_iso: With both copies carrying the violation, the per-copy validation reports SidecarParse for each copy (a Verifier reports both). The Recoverer finds no valid header/index copy, so its outcome for the epoch is SidecarMetadataUnavailable{epoch_id} (Section 13.3 step 4, Section 12.5).
conventions.erratum_to_frozen_concurrent_checks: Several frozen 7a cases mutate one copy only: sidecar-copy-generation, sidecar-copy-kind-reserved, sidecar-header-reserved variants a and b, sidecar-data-crc-count, sidecar-footer-index, sidecar-header-block-count, sidecar-inline-index-bytes, sidecar-logical-shard-count, sidecar-parity-block-count, sidecar-primary-start, sidecar-real-data-shard-count, sidecar-tail-start, sidecar-tape-uuid, sidecar-total-block-count a/b, sidecar-k-zero, sidecar-m-zero and sidecar-s-zero. Each of these also breaks the Section 9.1 primary/tail agreement rule ('only copy_kind and the recomputed CRCs differ'), and several frozen concurrent_checks lists do not say so. The three cases whose lists name no other rule at all (sidecar-copy-generation, sidecar-copy-kind-reserved, sidecar-header-reserved variant a) are included below.

not_isolatable.reason: At block 0 the only value that is both in the domain {1, 2} and consistent with the Section 13.3 step-2 copy-kind cross-check is 1; at block H+P it is 2. Any value that is 'neither primary nor tail' therefore also breaks the position cross-check in whichever block it sits. copy_kind is excluded from the hash and the agreement rule, so those are not involved.

Section 9.2 requires real_data_shard_count = end − start and real in 1..=S×k. Those two rules imply end > start, so any end ≤ start also breaks one of them: end = start forces real = 0, and end < start makes end − start underflow. The underflow is overflow-9.2-end-minus-start. The range is also mirrored in the footer, the directory and the map entry, but that is secondary.

k = 0 forces logical_shard_count = S×k = 0 if that rule is to hold, and then 'real in 1..=S×k' is an empty range, while real = end − start ≥ 1 because the range is non-empty. So the logical-count rule or the real-count rule must break alongside k ≠ 0.
As sidecar-k-zero: S = 0 forces S×k = 0 and empties 1..=S×k. (It also forces P = 0, which a rebuild could accommodate as in sidecar-m-zero/isolated, but the real-count rule cannot be satisfied.)

A tape file has at least one block (Section 3.1), and the header total is validated against the measured count (Scanner item 5, Section 16.2). A total of 0 therefore always breaks the measured-count rule as well as 2H+P+1.

The footer total is compared with the measured count (the target) and with the header copies' total (Section 13.3 step 1). For the headers to agree they would need total 0, which breaks their own 2H+P+1 and measured-count rules. With the headers unreadable, the footer total 0 still disagrees with the map entry's block count 7, which is a third rule.

The forward mapping has no operation that can overflow: d = o − start cannot underflow once the covering descriptor is found. Its only hazard, S = 0, is division by zero rather than overflow, and S ≠ 0 is enforced by Section 9.2 (and S ≥ 1 by Section 6.6) in the same bytes.
end − start underflows exactly when end < start, which is the Section 9.2 'end > start' rule. The two conditions coincide, even at unit level.

The normative Section 9.4 algorithm has no operation that can overflow for any u64 inputs: offset stays ≤ block_size, and blocks grows by one per spill, so it stays below 2^64. A value of real_data_shard_count large enough to overflow a closed-form stream length (≥ 2^61) also breaks real ≤ S×k (S×k < 2^48 from the header widths). Only a non-normative closed form can overflow, with inputs B 262144, S 2, m 2, real 2^61.
total − 1 underflows only when total = 0, and total − 2 only when total ≤ 1. Both are exactly the values that 'required ≥ 2' forbids, so the underflow and that rule coincide.

A zero sidecar_total_block_count is itself a Section 10.1.5 decoder invariant violation (DirectoryInvalid), and it disagrees with the map entry's block count, so the rescue never reaches the subtraction.
T − W underflows exactly when W > T, which is the Section 14 step-2 'W ≤ T' rule. The two coincide, even at unit level.

not_isolatable.case: terminal-scope-scalars (variants b and c on multi-256k)
not_isolatable.reason: On a prefix where sidecars are present and every Object ordinal is protected, the recomputed T equals the recomputed W. Changing either scalar alone breaks both its recompute and W = T, and changing both together breaks both recomputes. Each rule is isolated instead on another prefix: isolated-2 (T recompute, minimal profile), isolated-3 (W = T) and isolated-4 (W recompute), the last two on a rebuilt prefix whose last Object is unprotected.

total = 2M + 1 and footer index 2M cannot overflow once the ParityMap minimum block size of 0xC8 holds. With B ≥ 200 and 0xC8 + L ≤ 2^64 − 1 (larger L overflows M itself, which is overflow-10.1.2-M), M ≤ ceil((2^64 − 1)/200) < 2^57, so 2M + 1 < 2^58. An overflow needs B < 0xC8, and that breaks the minimum block size in the same input. A ceil written as (x + B − 1)/B that overflows belongs to M's evaluation, not to 2M + 1.
